title: Symmetry and Parity of an Odd Polynomial
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Symmetry and Parity
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Test the function g(x) = x^3 + x algebraically to determine whether it is even, odd, or neither, and state its geometric symmetry.
finalAnswer: Odd function; symmetric with respect to the origin

steps.title: Evaluate the Function at -x
steps.explanation: Substitute -x into every instance of the independent variable x in the definition of g(x).
steps.why: Testing for symmetry requires computing the algebraic output under reflection across the y-axis.

steps.title: Simplify Using Power Rules of Negative Quantities
steps.explanation: Because 3 is an odd exponent, (-x)^3 = -x^3, and the linear term simplifies directly to -x.
steps.why: Odd integer powers preserve the negative sign: (-1)^n = -1 for odd integers n.

steps.title: Factor Out the Negative Sign
steps.explanation: Factoring -1 from both terms reveals that g(-x) equals the exact negative of the original formula g(x).
steps.why: The algebraic definition of an odd function is that g(-x) = -g(x) for all x in its domain.

steps.title: State Geometric Symmetry Conclusion
steps.explanation: Since g(-x) = -g(x) holds for all real numbers x, the function is odd. Geometrically, its graph possesses 180-degree rotational symmetry about the origin.
steps.why: An odd function satisfies the condition that if (x, y) is on the graph, then (-x, -y) is also on the graph.
